records.counterexample: s := []int{1,2,3}; t := s[1:]; t[0] = 9; return s[1] == 9 — Go observes the shared backing (true); a plain JS array reslice loses aliasing.
records.ordinaryTypescript: A plain T[] with slice() copies.
records.ordinaryMismatch: T[].slice() allocates a fresh array, so a write through the reslice is not observed by the original, and capacity/append growth aliasing is lost.

alternatives.rejected: loses backing-array aliasing and capacity semantics observable by append/reslice
selected by the planner only for owner-only regions with no shared view; the carrier is required whenever a shared view or capacity is observed

records.smallestMechanism: a four-field record {backing, offset, length, capacity} over a shared backing array; nil is undefined
records.performanceEvidence: native-array selection removes the carrier for owner-only regions; the 10/2070 native distribution is recorded per region in the representation plan
invalidation: a region loses its shared-view or capacity requirement
the planner selects the native array for the region
records.acceptance: accepted: Go's slice aliasing, capacity, and reslice identity are runtime-observable and inexpressible by a copying plain array
reopening: TypeScript gains an addressable shared-view array primitive
the selected program no longer observes slice aliasing or capacity in any region

records.counterexample: x := 1; p := &x; *p = 2; return x == 2 — Go observes the write through the pointer (true); a captured value copy does not.
records.ordinaryMismatch: A plain binding cannot be aliased: taking its address and mutating through the pointer would not be observed by the original variable.

alternatives.rejected: selected for every variable whose address is never taken; the cell is introduced only for address-taken locals
still requires a boxed storage cell to alias a scalar local

records.smallestMechanism: a one-field cell {v} introduced only when a local's address is taken
records.performanceEvidence: cells are introduced only for address-taken locals, verified by the boxing scan; unboxed locals bind directly
invalidation: a local's address is no longer taken anywhere
records.acceptance: accepted: Go pointer aliasing to a scalar local is runtime-observable and inexpressible by a plain binding
reopening: the boxing scan proves a variable's address is never taken

records.counterexample: var p *T; var v any = p; return v == nil — Go's interface carries dynamic type *T with nil data, so the result is false; a plain undefined representation loses the dynamic type and returns true.
records.ordinaryTypescript: A direct union of the concrete branch types without a type tag.
records.ordinaryMismatch: An untagged union cannot distinguish typed nil from nil interface, cannot answer a type assertion between two types with the same storage, and cannot dispatch a method or interface equality by dynamic type.

alternatives.rejected: selected when dynamic behavior is unobservable; the box is required when typed nil, assertions, equality, or open dispatch is observed
two defined types with the same primitive storage collapse, losing assertion/equality/dispatch identity

records.smallestMechanism: a two-field box {r, v} where r is a canonical per-type rtti token; method, assertion, and equality dispatch is a generated exhaustive token switch (no method table, no name lookup)
records.performanceEvidence: dispatch is a direct token switch of typed calls with no runtime member lookup; the rtti carries no method table
invalidation: a region's dynamic type is statically known at every site (direct value)
the reachable dynamic-type set cannot be proven closed (fail closed)
records.acceptance: accepted: Go interface dynamic type, typed nil, assertion, equality, and dispatch are runtime-observable and inexpressible by an untagged value
reopening: a region proves its dynamic type is unobservable
the reachable dynamic-type set is no longer closed

records.counterexample: m := map[key]V{}; m[key{1,2}] = v; return m[key{1,2}] — Go keys structs by value; a JS Map keys objects by identity, so a fresh equal key misses.
records.ordinaryTypescript: A JS Map<K, V> keyed directly.
records.ordinaryMismatch: A JS Map keys object and struct keys by reference identity, not by Go's value equality, so two equal-but-distinct struct keys are treated as different.

alternatives.rejected: scalar keys work but struct/array keys must key by value, which Map does by identity
coerces keys to strings and cannot represent non-string Go key types

records.smallestMechanism: a Map<string, [K, V]> whose string key is the type's injective canonical encoding, retaining the original key for range
records.performanceEvidence: scalar-keyed maps use the direct string/number key; the composite encoding is used only for struct/array keys
invalidation: a map's key type is a scalar with a direct JS key
records.acceptance: accepted: Go value-equality map keys are runtime-observable and inexpressible by identity-keyed JS Maps
reopening: the selected program uses only scalar map keys
